skills.name: oods-lake
skills.why: The lake's own skill: migrations, time travel and recovery, maintenance, `checks.sql` as a gate, the R2 tokens and bucket rules
skills.caveat: Stacks on marola-dev/marola-oods#22; its first PR (#24) closed unmerged

skills.name: oods-lake-reviewer
skills.why: Read-only review of a MIP-0075 diff against the lake's invariants: one writer, upload before export, no persistent secret, inlining off, applied migrations never edited, no glob over `lake/`
skills.caveat: Reports, never edits; a person decides

skills.name: cloudflare
skills.why: Cloudflare's own product map, with `references/r2/` (S3 API, tokens, lifecycle, limits, pricing, gotchas)
skills.caveat: Points at live docs, not facts; R2 setup stays a person's (MIP-0075 §5.6)

skills.name: s3-explore
skills.why: Lists the bucket and reads Parquet metadata without downloading data (`read_blob` without `content`, `parquet_metadata`)
skills.caveat: Its R2 row is a `TYPE R2` secret on `r2://`; the lake uses `TYPE s3` on `s3://` (§4.4). Its `FROM '<glob>'` preview returns wrong rows on `lake/` after an update: list and read metadata only, query through an attach

skills.name: attach-db
skills.why: Attaches a local copy of `oods.ducklake` and keeps the session for `query`
skills.caveat: Its `state.sql` may hold secrets in plain text: attach `READ_ONLY`, keep the R2 secret out of it

skills.name: query
skills.why: Runs SQL on the attached lake (`beach_point`, `fetch_run`, `AT (VERSION => n)`); sets `allow_persistent_secrets=false`
skills.caveat: Read-only by use, not by design: the attach must be `READ_ONLY`

skills.name: duckdb-docs
skills.why: Full-text search over the DuckDB and DuckLake docs, so an answer cites the version the lake pins
skills.caveat: Downloads the search indexes and installs `httpfs` and `fts` locally; never in a job

skills.name: motherduck-ducklake
skills.why: DuckLake maintenance as explicit operations (`ducklake_flush_inlined_data`, `merge_adjacent_files`), the single-writer reality, the version matrix
skills.caveat: Written for MotherDuck: keep the DuckLake parts, drop the product's

skills.name: iceberg
skills.why: The Inspect first, Decide, Safety, Verify shape; retention windows, orphan cleanup, rollback
skills.caveat: Iceberg, not DuckLake: structure and rules only

skills.name: hops-table-maintenance
skills.why: Evidence from a script, a reviewable plan, approval per destructive step, dry run, before and after
skills.caveat: Spark and feature groups: the workflow only

skills.name: b2-cloud-storage
skills.why: Object-store safety rules (read-only by default, dry run and an explicit yes before a delete, never public) and the size and cost audit
skills.caveat: Re-point from B2 to R2: no versioning, no spend cap

skills.name: troubleshooting-dbt-job-errors
skills.why: Diagnosing a failed scheduled job from its logs, history and data, and "never modify a test to make it pass" (for `checks.sql`)
skills.caveat: dbt Cloud: map its logs and API to the Actions run and `fetch_run`

skills.name: security-audit
skills.why: A security review of the ETL workflows and the `oods` module, which hold the R2 write token
skills.caveat: Run its full workflow only on an explicit audit request; findings go to a person

left_out.name: wrangler
left_out.why: The lake uses the AWS CLI and DuckDB's S3 API, not Wrangler; the bucket and tokens are a person's. A fit for marola-site's Worker (#12)

left_out.name: basin
left_out.why: R2 Iceberg tables through Basin Catalog: a different table format and a paid product path, rejected by MIP-0075 §4.4

left_out.name: install-duckdb
left_out.why: Installs extensions from the network; MIP-0075 row 2 pins them by sha256 and a job never downloads code

left_out.name: motherduck-connect, motherduck-security-governance
left_out.why: MotherDuck's service, which the lake does not use
